faqs.question: What are good Halloween Pictionary words for kids?
faqs.answer: Pick single objects a child can draw from memory, such as eyeball, bone, coffin, lollipop, skull or worm. All six score 3 out of 3 for drawability on this page's scale. Whisper the word to children who cannot read yet.

faqs.question: How long should each turn be in a Halloween drawing game?
faqs.answer: Sixty seconds suits a party. It is double the 30-second limit used in a 2023 Nature Communications drawing study, where players were paid a bonus for speed, and party guests are not.

faqs.question: Can you write letters or numbers in Pictionary?
faqs.answer: No. Letters, numbers, talking, sounds and gestures are all out, the same drawer rules a 2018 classroom study used. Arrows, plus signs and blank dashes showing word count are normally allowed, but tally marks count as numbers.

faqs.question: How do I run Halloween Pictionary over a video call?
faqs.answer: Send the secret word to the drawer by private message, then have them draw on the call's whiteboard or share a drawing app on screen. Test the setup the day before, and give phone players words scored 2 or 3.

faqs.question: Is Pictionary a trademark?
faqs.answer: Yes. USPTO Reg. 1,392,492, filed on 28 March 1985 and registered on 6 May 1986, covers PICTIONARY for a board game and lists Pictionary Incorporated as owner. Call a home-made version a Halloween drawing game on flyers.

faqs.question: Does Mattel own Pictionary?
faqs.answer: The USPTO record names Pictionary Incorporated, of Nevada, as owner of the core board-game mark. That company shares a street address in El Segundo with Mattel, Inc., which registered PICTIONARY PIC-TATO on 24 March 2026.

faqs.question: How many words do I need for a Halloween Pictionary night?
faqs.answer: For two teams of 4 to 6, about 36 words covers three laps of Easy, Medium and Hard with spares. Keep a few extra Easy words for anyone joining late.

faqs.question: What happens when nobody guesses the word in time?
faqs.answer: No one scores, and the word goes back in the pile for a later bonus round. Repeated drawings usually need fewer strokes the second time, as a 2023 study of 69 drawing pairs found.

faqs.question: Does drawing a word help you remember it?
faqs.answer: Yes, in lab studies. A 2021 Psychonomic Bulletin & Review paper found drawing a word beat writing it for later recall, for abstract words as well as concrete ones, with a slightly bigger benefit for concrete words.

faqs.question: Can grandparents and young children play on the same team?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pair a confident drawer with each older player and start with the Easy tier. Offer a guessing-only role to anyone with a tremor or limited hand control.

faqs.question: When is Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is 31 October every year. It falls on a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027, so a weekend game night works either year.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Pictionary Words, Rated by How Easy They Are to Draw

Halloween Pictionary is a team drawing game. One player gets 60 seconds to sketch a spooky word with no letters, numbers or talking, and their team guesses until someone says it exactly. Below are 36 original Halloween Pictionary words in three tiers, each scored for drawability with the wrong guess it usually gets first.

Online players need smaller asks. Phones carried 48.3% of all views of pages shared through SubhSandesh, and touch screens of any kind 48.4%, so in a similar group roughly half your players will draw with a fingertip. This page also covers the rules, four setups compared, what drawing-game research shows, and who owns the "Pictionary" name.

## What is Halloween Pictionary, and who owns the name?

Halloween Pictionary is the sketch-and-guess party game played with Halloween words. Only the word list changes, and paper or a whiteboard replaces the board game.

"Pictionary" is a registered trademark, though, not a generic word. The [USPTO record for the board-game mark, Reg. 1,392,492](https://tsdr.uspto.gov/#caseNumber=73529303&caseType=SERIAL_NO&searchType=statusSearch) shows Robert S. Angel of Seattle filed it on 28 March 1985, after first use on 16 February 1985. It was registered on 6 May 1986 and now lists Pictionary Incorporated of Nevada as owner.

That owner's address is 333 Continental Boulevard, El Segundo, the same street address Mattel, Inc. gives on its PICTIONARY PIC-TATO registration of 24 March 2026. In December 2024 the owner even applied to use the name on clothing, Halloween costumes included. On a school newsletter or work flyer, "Halloween drawing game" is the safer label.

## 36 Halloween Pictionary words in three tiers

Each word has a drawability score. A 3 means one or two shapes carry it, a 2 needs a small scene, and a 1 needs a chain of pictures; these are editorial ratings, not measured times.

### Easy: single objects for ages 5 to 8

Each is one thing a child can draw from memory. Whisper words to players who cannot read yet.

- **Eyeball (3):** first wrong guess is "target"; add veins.
- **Bone (3):** reads as "dog biscuit" until both ends get knobbly.
- **Coffin (3):** a stretched six-sided box, "door" until a lid line appears.
- **Glow stick (3):** a bent tube with rays; "banana" comes first.
- **Lollipop (3):** a spiral on a stick, rarely missed.
- **Skull (3):** a rounded head with dark eye holes; "face" comes first.
- **Worm (3):** a wavy line with a face; "snake" comes first.
- **Gumball machine (2):** a ball of dots on a stand; "bubble tea" is the trap.
- **Haystack (2):** a dome of scribbles; "hedgehog" comes first.
- **Rat (2):** the long bare tail beats "mouse".
- **Crystal ball (2):** a circle on a stand with hovering hands; "snow globe" is the trap.
- **Bare tree (2):** crooked leafless branches; "hand" is the first guess.

### Medium: actions and scenes for ages 9 and up

These need two or three objects working together, so plan before the timer starts.

- **A hand rising from a grave (2):** ground line first, or it reads as "plant".
- **A ghost doing laundry (2):** a sheet with eyes on a washing line.
- **A monster under the bed (2):** bed first, eyes beneath; "cat" is the usual miss.
- **A tortoise dressed as a ghost (2):** a shell under a sheet; "mushroom" is the miss.
- **A sweet bag with a hole (2):** sweets trailing behind; "breadcrumbs" is the miss.
- **A thunderstorm over a castle (2):** zigzag lightning above turrets.
- **A haunted swing moving by itself (1):** an empty swing with motion lines; "playground" comes first.
- **Fog rolling across a lake (1):** wavy layers over water; expect "steam".
- **A vampire with no reflection (1):** a caped figure beside an empty mirror frame.
- **A creaking door (1):** motion lines and a frightened face carry the sound.
- **A lantern path through the woods (1):** trees, a dashed trail, small lights; "runway" is the miss.
- **A fortune teller reading a palm (1):** a lined hand and a headscarf; "nail salon" is the miss.

### Hard: abstract words and compound phrases for teens and adults

Split the phrase, draw each half, and join them with a plus sign. Plus signs and arrows are symbols, so they stay legal.

- **Ghostwriter (2):** a sheet ghost holding a pen.
- **Sweet tooth (2):** a tooth wearing a lollipop hat; "dentist" comes first.
- **Monster truck (2):** giant wheels and teeth on the grille.
- **Sugar rush (2):** a sweet, an arrow, a running figure.
- **Cold feet (2):** bare feet in ice cubes; "frostbite" is the miss.
- **Nightmare (1):** a crescent moon, a plus sign, a horse.
- **Goosebumps (1):** a goose, a plus sign, a bumpy arm.
- **Graveyard shift (1):** a grave beside a clock face with no numerals.
- **Dead end (1):** a road stopping at a wall, no sign lettering.
- **Spirit level (1):** a builder's level with a ghost in the bubble.
- **Costume malfunction (1):** a sheet costume with its eye holes in the wrong place.
- **Fear of the dark (1):** a switched-off light and a shaking stick figure.

## How to play: 60-second rules for two teams

Read these 5 rules aloud before the first turn, because disputes are easier to settle then than mid-round.

1. Split into two teams of 2 to 6 players and write the 36 words on folded slips.
2. The drawer reads one slip, then gets 60 seconds on a phone timer.
3. No letters, numbers, talking, sounds or gestures. Arrows, plus signs and blank dashes for word count are allowed.
4. The team must say the exact phrase. "Swing" does not score "a haunted swing moving by itself".
5. Play one lap per tier, Easy to Hard, scoring 1, 2 and 3 points.

For a faster version, both teams' drawers sketch the same word at once and the first correct team scores. A [2018 study of that simultaneous format by Kara Mosovsky at Moravian College](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC6289827) surveyed 64 students over three semesters: all called it fun, 98% would recommend it, and 94% rated it an effective review method. Its drawer rules match ours: no talking, sounds, gestures, numbers or letters.

Our 60 seconds doubles the 30-second limit in the Stanford study below. The extra time keeps the Hard tier fair for party guests.

## Same room or online: 4 ways to play compared

This compares four setups by group size, kit and best tiers. The figures are our recommendations, not tested limits.

| Setup | Players | Kit | Best tiers | Main snag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper pads at a table | 4 to 10 | A5 pads, thick pens, timer | All three | Small drawings across a table |
| Whiteboard or easel | 6 to 16 | One board, 2 marker colours | Medium, Hard | One drawer at a time |
| Video call, laptops | 4 to 12 | Shared whiteboard or screen share | All three | Lag eats into the 60 seconds |
| Video call, mostly phones | 3 to 8 | Fingertip and a drawing app | Easy, Medium | Fine detail is hard |

The smaller the drawing surface, the more you should lean on Easy words.

Online, send each secret word to the drawer by private message, never in the group chat. Most video-call apps offer a whiteboard or screen sharing, but features change, so test yours the day before.

Because about half of shared-page views on SubhSandesh come from phones, assume remote guests are similar until they say otherwise. Give phone players words scored 2 or 3, and save the 1s for anyone with a mouse or stylus.

## Why some Halloween words take longer to draw

Drawability comes down to whether one shape can stand for the whole idea. In a [2023 Nature Communications study by Hawkins, Sano, Goodman and Fan](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10110538), 138 participants formed 69 pairs and played a Pictionary-style reference game with a 30-second drawing limit. Strokes per drawing fell steadily as pairs repeated objects, yet the sketches kept the features that set each object apart.

So the Hard tier gets easier late in the night. Repeat a word as a bonus round and your team will often crack it with fewer lines.

Drawing also helps memory, an effect Jeffrey Wammes and colleagues have studied since 2016. A [2021 Psychonomic Bulletin & Review paper by Roberts and Wammes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32939630/) found drawing a word beat writing it for later recall, from concrete words to abstract ones, with a slightly larger benefit for concrete words. This page relied on the abstract alone.

## Two Halloween pages for whoever skipped the drawing game

Neither page runs a game, so there are no invites and no scoreboard. Each one speaks to a single recipient, such as the friend who skipped your drawing night.

The [jack-o'-lantern carving card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is the quicker build: about 5 minutes, six photo slots, and a closing boo question the recipient cannot refuse. The [premium page that plays your recorded voice](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) needs roughly 10 minutes; it allows a 60-second voice message, 12 photos, a timed unlock and one written reply back to you.

When that friend is far away and the holiday is a pretext, a [miss-you page built around open-when letters](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits better. Across SubhSandesh, 38.5% of creators lock their page behind a password, and 90.9% of pages that get started are eventually shared.

## When a drawing game is the wrong pick

A drawing game rewards fast hands. Offer guessing-only roles to players with a tremor or limited hand control, and in a mixed-age family pair a confident drawer with each grandparent.

There is a memory nuance too. A [2024 Memory & Cognition editorial by Bainbridge, Chamberlain, Wammes and Fan](https://research.gold.ac.uk/id/eprint/37520/3/Bainbridge%20et%20al%20%282024%29%20special-issue-editorial.pdf) summarises work finding that drawing improved associative memory in younger adults but only item memory in older adults. For older players, treat the game as fun rather than a brain workout.

Above about 12 guessers, people shout over each other, so split into three teams. SubhSandesh loses here too: its interface is English only, it keeps no scoreboard and it cannot host the game.

## Sources

- Mosovsky K., *J Microbiol Biol Educ* 19(3), 14 December 2018.
- Hawkins R.D. et al., *Nature Communications* 14, 17 April 2023.
- Roberts B.R.T. and Wammes J.D., *Psychonomic Bulletin & Review* 28(1), online 16 September 2020 (abstract only).
- Bainbridge W.A. et al., *Memory & Cognition*, 27 August 2024 (author copy).
- USPTO, PICTIONARY Reg. 1,392,492, record checked 14 October 2026.
